The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
The `StringUtils.join(Object[], String)` method in the Apache Commons Lang library handles joining an array of objects into a single string with a specified separator. The method first checks if the input array is null, and if so, it returns null. 

In the failing test case `testJoin_Objectarray`, the test is trying to join an array of objects and expects the result to be the string "null". This test fails because one of the objects in the array has a `toString` method that returns null. The actual result returned by `StringUtils.join` is null, not the string "null" as expected in the test.

To fix this issue, the `StringUtils.join` method needs to handle cases where the `toString` method of an object returns null. One possible solution is to check for null values in the `toString` method of each object before joining. Another option is to provide a default string value to use when the `toString` method returns null.

The root cause of the issue is the assumption made in the test case that the `StringUtils.join` method will handle the toString method of objects that return null gracefully.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.

messages.content:
The issue with `StringUtils.join(Object[], String)` can be fixed by modifying the method `StringUtils.join(Object[], String)` to handle cases where the `toString()` method of an object in the array returns null. Here is the method that needs to be fixed:

```java
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.join(Object[] array, String separator)
```

This method should be updated to handle null values returned by the `toString()` method of objects in the array to prevent the NullPointerException that is currently occurring.
